⇒ __**16 × 17**__ + 16 + 3 - 8 = 60

⇒ 272 + 16 + 3 - 8

⇒ 291 - 8

⇒ 283

(4) **17 and 16, − and ×**

⇒ 3 − 17 + 3 + 16 × 8 = 60

After interchanging the sign and number:

⇒ __**3 × 16**__ + 3 + 17 - 8 = 60

⇒ 48 + 3 + 17 - 8

questions.question: The central bank may ________ to discourage credit in the economy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**increase bank rate.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **The bank rate** is the interest rate at which the central bank **lends money** to commercial banks.
 
• When the central bank** increases the bank rate**, it becomes **more expensive** for commercial banks to borrow money from the central bank.
 
• This, in turn,** reduces** the amount of credit that commercial banks can offer to their customers, thereby **discouraging credit** in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Increasing **the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is another tool that the central bank can use to** discourage credit.**

 
 
• **CRR **is the amount of funds that commercial banks have to keep with the central bank as a** percentage of their deposits**.
 
• When the **CRR is decreased**, banks have more funds available to lend, which can lead to an** increase in credit** in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Buying securities** in the open market is a tool that the central bank can use to **increase liquidity** in the economy.
 
 
• When the central bank buys securities, it i**njects money** into the economy, which can lead to an** increase in credit.**
 
• Therefore, this option is** not** suitable for discouraging credit in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Reducing** the **Statutory Liquidity Ratio** (SLR) is another tool that the central bank can use to **increase the availability of funds** for banks to lend.
 
 
• SLR is the percentage of deposits that banks have to keep in the form of liquid assets such as** cash, gold, or government securities.**
 
• When the SLR is** reduced**, banks have** more funds available** to lend, which can lead to an increase in credit in the economy.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT come under the Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India?

options.text: Safeguard public property and to abjure violence
Cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom
Uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Exercise adult franchise.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Fundamental Duties** are enshrined in **Part IV-A **of the Constitution and were added by the **42nd Amendment in 1976.**
 
• There are **11 Fundamental Duties** listed in** Article 51-A,** which are **non-justiciable **in nature, meaning that they **cannot be enforced** by law.
 
• The exercise of the adult franchise is** not** a Fundamental Duty, but rather a Right given to citizens under **Article 326** of the Constitution.
 
• **51(A)(a)**: Abide by the Constitution, respect its ideals, the National Flag, and the National Anthem.
 
• **51(A)(b):** Cherish and follow ideals from the national struggle for freedom.
 
• **51(A)(c):** Uphold the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• **51(A)(d): **Defend the country and render national service when required.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exercise adult franchise **refers to the **right to vote** in elections, which is a key feature of a **democratic system.**
 
• **Safeguarding public property and abjuring violence** is important for maintaining **law and order** in the country.
 
• **Cherishing and following the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom** is a way of paying **homage to the leaders** and movements that fought for India's independence.
 
• **Upholding and protecting the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India** is crucial for maintaining **national security and preventing any threats** to the country's territorial integrity.

• Halite forms** isometric crystals.**

questions.question:
Which of the following modern industries was in operation in India during British rule?

a. Cotton

b. Jute

c. Iron and Steel

options.text: All of a, b and c

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All of a, b, and c.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cotton, jute, and iron and steel** were all modern industries that were in operation in** India** during British rule.
 
• **Cotton **was one of the most important industries during this time, with India being one of the** largest cotton producers** in the world.
 
• The British established** cotton mills** in India to process the **raw cotton** and **export the finished products** back to Britain.
 
• **Jute** was another important industry, with India being the **largest producer** of jute in the world.
 
• Jute mills were established in** Bengal **to process the raw jute and export the finished products.
 
• **Iron and steel production** also began to develop in India during the British rule.
 
• The Tata Iron and Steel Company was established in** 1907** and became one of the** largest steel producers** in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other modern industries that developed during British time included** tea production, mining, and railway construction.**
 
• By building the** third-largest railroad network** in the world, the British brought India together and made it possible for it to develop a modern economy.
 
• India was able to modernize thanks to the construction of **telephone and telegraph lines, road networks, irrigation systems, dams, bridges, and canals.**
 
• The founding of the cotton textile industry in **Bombay in 1854** marked the beginning of India's modern industrial sector in an organized manner.

questions.question: A boat can cover 120 km upstream and back in a total of 30 hours, and 25 km upstream and 40 km downstream in a total of 7 hours. How much distance will the boat cover in 16 hours in still water?
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

A boat can cover 120 km upstream and back in a total of 30 hours.

A boat can cover 25 km upstream and 40 km downstream in a total of 7 hours.

FORMULA USED:

Distance = Speed × Time 

Speed in upstream = Speed of boat in still water - Speed in current water

Speed in downstream = Speed of boat in still water + Speed in current water 

CALCULATION:

Let the speed of the boat in still water be x km/h and the speed of the boat in current water be y km/h 

Speed in downstream = x + y , Speed in upstream = x - y 

Now, Distance/Speed = Time 

⇒ 120/(x +y) + 120/(x -y) = 30 .........(1)

Also,

⇒ 40/(x +y) + 25/(x -y) = 7 ...........(2)

Now, on multiplying eq(2) by 3 and subtracting eq(1) it from we get

⇒ 120/(x +y) + 120/(x -y) - 120/(x +y) - 75/(x -y) = 30 - 21

⇒ 45/( x -y) = 9

⇒( x -y) = 5 ..........eq(3)

Putting eq(3) in eq(1):

⇒ 120/(x +y) + 120/5 = 30 

⇒ 120/(x +y) = 30 - 24

⇒ (x +y) = 20 .......eq(4)

Solving both eq(3) and eq(4), we get:

⇒ x = 12.5

Distance the boat cover in 16 hours in still water = 12.5 × 16

⇒ 200 km.

**The distance the boat cover in 16 hours in still water is 200km.**

questions.question: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 500 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the rate of 17 km/h and 20 km/h, respectively. What is the distance between them after 8 minutes?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed in same direction = 20 − 17 = 3 km/h.

Convert relative speed to m/min = 3 × (1000/60) = 50 m/min.

Distance reduced in 8 minutes = 50 × 8 = 400 m.

Remaining distance = 500 − 400 = 100 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 
• 
 
 Policeman (P)
 20 km/h
 
 Thief (T)
 17 km/h
 

 Initial Gap = 500 m
 

 

 Relative Motion Diagram

Given:

Initial distance = 500 m

Speed of Policeman (Sₚ) = 20 km/h

Speed of Thief (Sₜ) = 17 km/h

Time (t) = 8 minutes

Formula used: Distance = Relative Speed × Time

Relative speed (same direction) = Sₚ − Sₜ

⇒ Relative speed = 20 − 17 = 3 km/h

⇒ Speed in m/min = (3 × 1000) ÷ 60 = 50 m/min

⇒ Distance covered in 8 minutes = 50 × 8 = 400 m

⇒ Distance between them after 8 minutes = Initial distance − Relative distance covered

⇒ Distance = 500 − 400 = 100 m

**∴ The correct answer is 100 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference (S₁ − S₂). In opposite directions, it is the sum (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert km/h to m/min, multiply by 1000/60 or 50/3.

Catching Time

Time to catch = Initial Distance ÷ Relative Speed. The distance covered by policeman until catching = Sₚ × Catching Time.</p

questions.question: P takes twice as long as Q or three times as long as R to complete a task. If they work together, they can complete the task in two days. How long will it take Q to complete the task on his own?

Efficiency = Total work/Time taken

Calculation:

⇒ Time taken by Q = 3 units

⇒ Time taken by R = 2 units

⇒ Efficiency of P = 6/6 = 1 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of Q = 6/3 = 2 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of R = 6/2 = 3 unit/day

Total efficiency = (1 + 2 + 3) = 6 units/day

They complete the task in 2 days,

Thus, Q takes total time,

⇒ 12/2 = 6 days

**It takes 6 days for Q to complete the task on his own.**
